independent.summary: An operation whose `tags` is not a sequence crashes the parse: `toJS(...)` returns a string (or plain object) for `tags: Pets` / `tags: {a: b}`, `?? []` does not replace it, and `.filter` is not a function — a TypeError escapes `parseOpenApi`, so `POST /drafts/openapi` answers 500 with a raw stack message instead of the 400/drop-reason the producer promises for a malformed document.

`decodeURIComponent(raw)` in `resolveLocalRef` throws URIError on a ref segment containing a stray `%` (e.g. `$ref: "#/components/pathItems/50%off"`), which escapes the parse as a non-OpenApiParseError and becomes a 500 — the item and docs state an unresolvable ref must be a drop reason, and the surrounding code is written to return a reason string for every other bad ref.

BraindumpInput.test.js explicitly covers the both-keys case: `expect(producerFor('openapi: 3.0.0
services:
  - name: x
')).toBe('openapi')`.
The message names all three keys the file could have had, which is the stated intent; wording is a preference, not a defect.
`filename` is only used as a log label and a 60-char draft title — nothing writes a file, so traversal is impossible; it is also type-checked as a string.
The version gate at openApi.js:222-228 throws `OpenApiParseError` naming `openapi: 4.0.0` etc., and the route maps that to a 400; a unit test asserts it.
`doc.errors` is checked first and raises a line-numbered `Invalid JSON or YAML` 400, and non-mapping content hits the explicit `top level ... is not a mapping` refusal.
`new URL('https://a.example/v2?x=1')` yields hostname `a.example`; only genuinely relative URLs resolve against the `relative.invalid` base and correctly return null.
The comment lists producers still to come (drift/repo/k8s) and was deliberately updated because `openapi` graduated into the enum; it matches the code.
The factory calls `parse(source, { existingEntities: roster, lineOffset })` — both options are passed, and both default anyway.
`parseOpenApi` is imported at the top of the same diff hunk from `../lib/producers/openApi.js`, which the diff also adds.
`OpenApiParseError` is exported by the new openApi.js and imported in the same import statement shown in the diff.
`MAX_OPENAPI_CHARS` is exported from openApi.js (= `MAX_COMPOSE_CHARS`) and imported in the diff; the route also reads it via `maxChars`, not directly.
`resolveLocalRef` returns the string `"... is not defined in this document"`, which the caller turns into a drop reason; a unit test asserts exactly that.
The re-import test does assert `item.matchedBy === 'exact-normalized-title'` for every entity item.
The test's claim is that a re-import proposes updates rather than copies, and it verifies op, matchedBy, targetEntityId and pruned blocks; applying the second draft is not what it claims to test.
Backwards: a near-miss must stay `op: 'create'` (never merged), and the test asserts precisely that plus the `duplicate_candidate` flag.
That test is scoped to the item cap being a no-op; the fixture's parse is asserted in detail by the tests in the 'openapi fixture' describe block.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication or authorization code changes; the new route inherits `requireAuth` + `resolveWorkspace` already mounted on `/drafts` in app.js.
Credential handling is central — the uploaded spec goes through `redactSecrets` at the route seam and the fixture carries an example API key asserted never to be stored.
The producer is deterministic with no model call, and no allowance, quota or billing code is touched.
The change only creates draft rows; no deletion or overwrite path is added or modified, and the applier is untouched.
Nothing in the diff makes a network call — it parses a document that describes APIs, which is not the same as calling one.
No build, deploy, CI or version configuration is changed.

summary: Every one of the 16 local findings is a false positive — most assert that symbols imported in the diff are undefined or that assertions the tests plainly make are absent — and the triage is wrong on three of six categories, while both genuine defects (malformed-input paths that return 500 instead of a 400/drop reason) were missed.
